selection: First three lexicographically ordered saved annotations created after the resumed blog sweep began, frozen before reading their text. No content, syntax-flag or detector-score selection. This is a small development inspection, not a representative accuracy sample.
dependency_inspection: Selected complete token/head tables for a contracted copula, discourse-marker coordination, a result coordination, a quoted clause modifying a noun, and an auxiliary-led question. Other attachments remain unreviewed.
input_comparison: Existing Rust CommonMark view, whole-document raw/rendered pairs. The new small-parser raw token and sentence arrays matched all three saved paragraph-documents-v1 annotations; profile identities remain distinct.

reproducibility_check.method: Reran the same frozen Rust binary and transformer parser with the three inputs in reverse order and one identical duplicate, yielding eight annotations.
reproducibility_check.scope: The observed errors reproduce under this changed order. This does not establish universal determinism or identify the cause of within-document context sensitivity.

findings.observation: The transformer recovers a contracted copula and its subject/adjectival predicate where the small parser treats the contraction as possession. It also recovers the nominal head outside a quoted clause, and the verb and subject of an auxiliary-led question. These improvements occur in both raw and rendered views.

Decoding HTML spaces restores several intended sentence boundaries in one diary post and removes lexical analyses of trailing entity names. Offset correctness is verified separately from the grammatical judgments.

In the same post, the rendered transformer analysis changes a previously plausible result coordination into a clausal complement with its connector attached to punctuation. The words of this sentence are unchanged; entity replacements occur later in the document. The internal cause has not been isolated.

In a question compilation, the raw transformer already merges several independent questions and a closing statement. After decoding only trailing HTML spaces, it merges two further closing sentences into that span. The small parser retains these boundaries but has other tagging and quoted-speech boundary errors.

The transformer retains whitespace-only sentences and splits an emoticon into separate sentence spans. Interjections, elliptical fragments and informal spelling also occur legitimately; a missing finite verb alone is not evidence of a parser failure. Mojibake remains unrepaired.

One post explicitly attributes most of its content to another source and distinguishes a short added portion. Blog account identity therefore does not establish sole authorship of its text. This observation does not verify the external attribution or estimate corpus-wide quotation prevalence.

next_action: Keep both parser profiles and current fitted spaces unchanged. Isolate sentence-boundary sensitivity with individual entity substitutions and unchanged context controls, and record quotation/attribution evidence before using posts as author-profile samples. Do not automatically repair every parser disagreement or treat fragments as errors.
limitations: Manual scope is full-text reading, every sentence span/root, and selected dependencies. Mechanical projection checks do not certify syntax or meaning. No general parser, author-attribution, detector or gradient improvement has been established. No default, feature denominator, corpus label or active fit changed.
